q: How does the Agile Practice Guide describe agile?
options: A mindset defined by four values, guided by twelve principles and shown through many practices
A single methodology with fixed steps
explanation: Agile is a mindset defined by the Agile Manifesto values, guided by its principles and enabled by various practices that teams select based on their needs.

q: Which of the following is one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
options: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
Following a plan over responding to change
explanation: The four values favor individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration and responding to change. The other options reverse the values.

q: The Agile Manifesto values "working software over comprehensive documentation". What does this mean?
options: Documentation still has value, but a working product is valued more
Documentation must be complete and approved before any of the work can start
explanation: The Manifesto says there is value in the items on the right, but the items on the left are valued more. Agile teams still document; they do not let documentation replace a working result.

q: According to the agile principles, what is the highest priority?
options: Satisfying the customer through early and continuous delivery of value
explanation: The first principle states that the highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of something valuable.

q: A sponsor asks an agile team how far along it is. One member offers the percentage of budget spent; another offers the number of documents approved. According to the agile principles, what is the primary measure of progress?
explanation: A working, functional deliverable that provides value is the primary measure of progress in agile.

q: Late in an agile project the customer asks for a significant change to a feature. How should the team respond?
options: Reject it, because the scope is fixed
Send it to the change control board and wait for a formal decision
Welcome it and have the product owner prioritize it in the backlog
Add it secretly without telling the product owner
explanation: The agile principles welcome changing requirements, even late in development. Change is handled by reprioritizing the backlog, not through a formal change control process.

q: A company is choosing work for its first agile team. One candidate is the routine monthly payroll run; another is a new product whose design nobody has attempted before. Which type of work is agile best suited to?
options: High-uncertainty work involving new design and problem-solving
Definable work with clear procedures proven on many past projects
explanation: High-uncertainty projects have high rates of change, complexity and risk. Agile approaches explore feasibility in short cycles and adapt quickly from feedback.

q: A team shows the customer rough, unfinished prototypes several times and improves the design after each round. Which characteristic is this?
explanation: Iterations allow feedback on partially completed or unfinished work in order to improve and modify it.

q: A team delivers a finished, usable part of the product to the customer every month. Which characteristic is this?
explanation: Increments provide finished deliverables that the customer may be able to use immediately.

q: How do agile approaches relate to iterative and incremental approaches?
options: Agile is neither iterative nor incremental
Agile combines both: the team iterates over the product to create finished increments
explanation: Agile approaches use both iterative and incremental characteristics, which gives early feedback and frequent delivery of value.

q: How long is an iteration in a typical agile approach?
explanation: Some agile approaches use iterations that are generally 1 to 4 weeks long, with a demonstration of what was accomplished at the end of each.

q: Which statement about planning is correct?
options: Planning happens only at the end of a project
All approaches plan; they differ in how much planning is done and when
explanation: Every life cycle includes planning. Predictive approaches plan as much as possible up front; agile teams plan and replan as information arrives from frequent deliveries.

q: What is the relationship between Lean, agile and Kanban?
options: Lean is a subset of Kanban
Agile and the Kanban Method are both descended from lean thinking
Kanban is a subset of Scrum
explanation: Lean thinking is the superset. Agile and the Kanban Method share lean concepts such as focus on value, small batch sizes and elimination of waste.

q: A support team wants to improve without changing its roles, titles or process on the first day. Which approach is known as the "start where you are" approach because a team can apply it to its existing way of working?
explanation: The Kanban Method is less prescriptive and less disruptive than some agile approaches, so teams can begin applying it with relative ease.

q: A team holds daily meetings and uses a task board, but delivers nothing to the customer for a year and resists every change. What is the best description?
options: The team is doing agile practices without an agile mindset
The team is using an incremental approach with fixed-length iterations
explanation: The agile mindset is about being agile, not simply doing agile. It means living the values: delivering value early, adapting quickly and learning from feedback.

q: A project will build a standard warehouse using a design the company has built twenty times. Requirements are stable. Which approach fits best?
options: Agile, because it is always better
explanation: For defined, repeatable projects with little uncertainty or likelihood of change, a predictive "plan the work, work the plan" approach is appropriate and efficient.

q: In which year was the Manifesto for Agile Software Development published?
explanation: Software industry thought leaders published the Manifesto in 2001, although many of the techniques existed years or decades earlier.

q: Which agile principle is the basis for the retrospective?
options: Working software is the primary measure of progress
At regular intervals the team reflects on how to become more effective and adjusts
Business people and developers work together daily
explanation: The twelfth principle asks the team to reflect at regular intervals on how to become more effective and then tune its behavior. The retrospective puts this into practice.

q: Two projects build similar software. One follows a predictive plan and the other an agile approach. When does each typically deliver business value?
options: Predictive: usually at the end. Agile: early and frequently.
Predictive: every week from the start. Agile: only at the end.
explanation: A serialized predictive project does not typically deliver business value until the end. Agile delivers the highest-value work first, which can give an earlier return on investment.

q: What does "simplicity" mean in the agile principles?
options: Using only the simplest tools that are available
Maximizing the amount of work not done
explanation: Simplicity is described as the art of maximizing the amount of work not done: avoid building what is not needed.

q: Which is an advantage of a predictive approach over an adaptive one?
options: Change is cheap at any point in the work
Plan, budget and dates are clear up front
Value reaches users every few weeks
A wrong requirement is found early
explanation: A predictive approach gives a clear plan, budget and dates at the start and suits stable requirements. Early delivery, cheap change and early discovery of problems are advantages of adaptive approaches.

q: An organization tries agile for the first time. Its people sit in separate departments that hand work to one another and are measured separately. Which organizational characteristic most hinders the adoption of agile approaches?
options: Staff dedicated to a single project
Executives who are willing to change
explanation: Work decomposed into departmental silos creates dependencies that prevent accelerated delivery. Safety, dedicated staff and executive willingness to change all support agility.

q: According to the Agile Practice Guide, what is the most important cultural norm for an organization trying a new way of working?
options: A detailed plan for every team
A bonus for the fastest team
explanation: The most important cultural norm in an organization willing to try any new method is enabling a safe work environment, in which people can reflect honestly on successes and failures.
